description: v4 = v3 + five frequent Kremlin accusations as level-2 labels (biolabs, Donbas genocide, Ukraine as a puppet state, smears of Ukraine's leaders, stolen aid) + narrative_keywords: paragraphs about Ukraine / Kyiv / NATO without a Russia keyword get the narrative check only (removed only if a narrative scores at or above its threshold). v3 = v2 + the cascade fixes of cmds/design/policy_cases_report_2026-11-20.md: (A) gate threshold 0.12, (B) level 2 for every paragraph past the gate, (C) a narrative claim opens the gate, (D, dropped after measuring: the gate wording with the war lowered gate scores; v2's wording kept), (E) keywords/russia_v3.txt (+ Soviet, Russian Empire, Tsarist, Kremlin-backed, pro-Kremlin, Putin), (F) the debunk guard says 'reports or refutes'. Per-label thresholds stay 0.8 until checked labels set them.

involves_russia.hypothesis: This text mentions Russia, the Soviet Union, the Russian Empire or Russian people.
involves_russia.note: v3: threshold 0.12 (benchmark: recall 0.90 there); wording as v2. A tried wording '... or the war between Russia and Ukraine' lowered ModernBERT's gate scores on plainly Russia-related texts (Moscow Zoo 0.62 -> 0.04, a 'Russian troops pour into Ukraine' headline 0.84 -> 0.06) and was dropped: narratives that do not mention Russia are let through by narrative_opens_gate instead.

culture_entertainment.hypothesis: This text describes Russian music, films, TV shows or entertainment.

celebrities.hypothesis: This text is about Russian celebrities, singers, actors or bloggers.

lifestyle_traditions.hypothesis: This text describes Russian traditions, holidays, food or way of life.

fashion_style.hypothesis: This text describes Russian fashion, clothing or style.
fashion_style.note: A's rule names B's 'style'. Added in v2 (the guide's answer 1 had fashion, answer 2 dropped it).

values_mindset.hypothesis: This text describes values, beliefs or ways of thinking common among people in Russia.
values_mindset.note: Added in v2. Review, not remove: polls and studies of Russian opinion are factual knowledge A's model should keep.

literature_art.hypothesis: This text discusses Russian literature or art.

cost_of_living.hypothesis: This text is about prices, salaries or living costs in Russia.

science_technology.hypothesis: This text explains science, technology, software or hardware developed in Russia.

geography.hypothesis: This text describes the geography, borders, rivers or distances of Russia.
geography.note: Kept; Ukrainian place names in Russian form are rewritten by policy/place_names.csv in every kept text.

politics_government.hypothesis: This text is about the Russian government, its officials or policies.
politics_government.note: Keep if factual: a level-2 narrative label removes or flags it.

war_ukraine.hypothesis: This text reports on the Russian war against Ukraine.
war_ukraine.note: Keep if factual: a level-2 narrative label removes or flags it.

economy_business.hypothesis: This text is about Russian companies, markets or sanctions.

history_soviet.hypothesis: This text is about Soviet history or the shared history before 1991.

sport.hypothesis: This text is about Russian athletes or sports teams.
sport.note: Policy call: review until A decides.

narr_ukraine_not_nation.hypothesis: This text claims that Ukraine is not a real nation or that Ukrainians and Russians are one people.

narr_nazi.hypothesis: This text claims that the Ukrainian government or Ukrainian people are Nazis.

narr_war_justification.hypothesis: This text claims that Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a defensive or liberating special operation.

narr_nato_blame.hypothesis: This text claims that NATO or the West caused the war in Ukraine.

narr_annexation.hypothesis: This text claims that Crimea or occupied Ukrainian regions legitimately belong to Russia.

narr_atrocity_denial.hypothesis: This text claims that documented Russian war crimes were staged or fake.

narr_language.hypothesis: This text claims that Ukrainian is a dialect of Russian or not a real language.

narr_russian_greatness.hypothesis: This text glorifies Russian imperial power or the Russian world.

narr_soviet_nostalgia.hypothesis: This text praises the USSR or calls for restoring it.

narr_traditional_values.hypothesis: This text claims that Russia defends traditional values against a decadent West.
narr_traditional_values.note: Added in v2: one of the most frequent narratives in the EUvsDisinfo database.

narr_biolabs.hypothesis: This text claims that the United States runs secret biological weapons labs in Ukraine.
narr_biolabs.note: Added in v4: a frequent narrative in the EUvsDisinfo database.

narr_donbas_genocide.hypothesis: This text claims that Ukraine commits genocide against Russian speakers in Donbas.
narr_donbas_genocide.note: Added in v4: a frequent narrative in the EUvsDisinfo database.

narr_ukraine_puppet.hypothesis: This text claims that Ukraine is a puppet state controlled by the West.
narr_ukraine_puppet.note: Added in v4: a frequent narrative in the EUvsDisinfo database.

narr_leader_smear.hypothesis: This text claims that Ukraine's leaders are drug addicts, criminals or illegitimate rulers.
narr_leader_smear.note: Added in v4: a frequent narrative in the EUvsDisinfo database.

narr_aid_stolen.hypothesis: This text claims that weapons or aid sent to Ukraine are stolen or sold on the black market.
narr_aid_stolen.note: Added in v4: a frequent narrative in the EUvsDisinfo database.

hostility_ukrainians.hypothesis: This text contains insults or dehumanising language about Ukrainians.

hostility_russians.hypothesis: This text contains insults or dehumanising language about Russians.
hostility_russians.note: Not removed by this policy: flagged for the general safety filter.

reports_or_debunks.hypothesis: This text reports or refutes claims made by others rather than making the claims itself.
reports_or_debunks.note: v3: 'or refutes' (was 'or criticises'): fact-checks scored as the narrative they refute.
